speaker: Doctor
text: Given the significantly elevated alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin with an enlarged gallbladder but no stones, do you have a history of alcohol use or have you experienced any recent fever or chills?

text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Smokes 1 pack of cigarettes per day and consumes 5 alcoholic beverages per day.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Alcoholic Cholecystitis (likely secondary to alcoholic hepatitis). The combination of significantly elevated ALP and bilirubin, an enlarged gallbladder without stones on ultrasound, and a social history of heavy alcohol use (5 drinks/day) strongly suggests alcoholic etiology rather than cholelithiasis.
